# Cedric Stanhope

## Overview

- **Age:** 16 years old  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States / Boston  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>

## Appearance

As a young child of ten, Cedric appeared smaller than his age, possessing a delicate face with crimson lips, dark blue eyes, and chestnut curls. By age thirteen he had grown quite tall for his age, and by sixteen he sported short-cut brown hair while continuing to grow taller.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c27 P23](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0023), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)_

## Personality

Cedric possesses a grave, reflective, and dreamy nature with a highly creative imagination and poetic thoughts. He is warm-hearted, polite, and deeply loving, showing intense devotion to his family and friends. Despite his fanciful mind, he is also manly, fair-minded, and capable of holding his own among his peers in games and sports.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), [v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009), [v2 c19 P26](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0026), [v2 c19 P32](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0032), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 c27 P5](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0005), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)_

## History

Cedric moved from the United States to Brierley to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope, and attend Brierley school under the instruction of Nell Harcourt. Upon starting school, he immediately bonded with Nell, becoming fast friends and one of her favorite pupils. He frequently brought her flowers, shared his inner imaginative thoughts, and confided in her about his deceased mother and his father, Stephen Stanhope. When his father visited Brierley, Cedric joyfully reunited with him and mentioned traveling to Welby to see Miss Rosalind Penrose, helping spark the rekindling of Stephen and Rosalind's past romance. Following his father's marriage to Rosalind, Cedric welcomed her into his life as 'Mother Rosalind' and spent time residing in Boston with them while returning to Echo Cottage and Brierley during the summer months. As he grew into a sixteen-year-old youth, his early childhood play with imaginary 'Rock People' faded into growing tall and playing football, though his close friendship with Nell remained unchanged.

## Quotes

> I ask you to take these, teacher, which I discovered in the field belonging to Mr. Duckett, and I returned so I could offer them to you since I believed you were a lady who would appreciate them, and also because . . . teacher, I am fond of you.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> It isn’t very easy to get acquainted with Father. I didn’t become really acquainted with him until my little mother had died. However, once you do come to know him, he is splendid. I love him most of all in the world, and then Grandma Stanhope, and after that, you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009)</sub>

> Am I out of my mind, do you believe?  <sub>[v2 c19 P12](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0012)</sub>

> Oh, Miss Harcourt, you can’t imagine what took place! Something truly wonderful. Father has arrived . . . only imagine that! Father has arrived! Step right inside. Father, this is my lovely teacher. You understand, father.  <sub>[v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021)</sub>

> However, I never address her simply as ‘mother,’ Because, as you understand, teacher, that title is reserved exclusively for my own dear mother, so I am unable to use it for anybody else. Instead, I address her as ‘Mother Rosalind’ and she is second in my affection only to father. In fact—I actually hold her slightly dearer than you, teacher.  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>
